subject: geog
source: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460) syllabus for examination in 2027, 2028 and 2029 — Cambridge International; Year 11 covers Paper 2 human geography (topics 6–10), geographical investigations and full-course revision

weeks.topic: Population growth and decline: birth rates, death rates and natural increase
objectives: Calculate natural increase
Explain causes of high and low birth and death rates
Describe world population growth

weeks.topic: The demographic transition model and population policies
objectives: Describe the stages of the demographic transition model
Evaluate pro-natalist and anti-natalist policies

weeks.topic: Population structures: youthful and ageing populations (detailed specific example)
objectives: Construct and interpret population pyramids
Explain dependency ratios
Evaluate responses to an ageing or youthful population

weeks.topic: International migration: push and pull factors
objectives: Classify types of migration
Explain push and pull factors and barriers

weeks.topic: Impacts of international migration (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain impacts on source and destination countries
Evaluate a specific migration flow

weeks.topic: Where people live: population distribution and density
objectives: Describe global patterns of population distribution
Explain physical and human factors affecting density

weeks.topic: Urbanisation: trends and causes
objectives: Describe global trends in urbanisation and megacities
Explain rural–urban migration

weeks.topic: Opportunities and challenges of urbanisation: informal settlements
objectives: Explain opportunities of city life
Describe challenges such as informal settlements, traffic and pollution

weeks.topic: Managing urban growth sustainably (detailed specific example)
objectives: Evaluate strategies such as self-help schemes and transport improvements
Assess a specific urban management example

weeks.topic: Measuring development: GNI, HDI and other indicators
objectives: Compare economic and social indicators of development
Classify countries as HICs, MICs and LICs

weeks.topic: The world is developing unevenly: causes and the development gap
objectives: Explain physical, economic and historical causes of uneven development
Describe inequality within countries

weeks.topic: Achieving sustainable development (detailed specific example)
objectives: Evaluate aid, fair trade and the Sustainable Development Goals
Assess a specific development project

weeks.topic: Changing employment structures: the Clark–Fisher model
objectives: Describe the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors
Apply the Clark–Fisher model to countries at different stages

weeks.topic: Globalisation and transnational corporations (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain factors driving globalisation
Evaluate the impacts of a specific TNC on host countries

weeks.topic: Review: populations, towns and cities, development and employment
objectives: Revise population pyramids and urban issues
Practise Paper 2 Section A questions

weeks.topic: Tourism as a growing industry (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain the growth of tourism
Evaluate benefits and costs and sustainable tourism

weeks.topic: How food is produced: farming systems
objectives: Describe farming systems as inputs, processes and outputs
Compare commercial and subsistence, arable and pastoral farming

weeks.topic: Global patterns of food supply and demand
objectives: Describe global patterns of food production and consumption
Explain factors increasing food demand

weeks.topic: Challenges of food supply: food insecurity (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain causes and impacts of food shortages
Evaluate solutions such as irrigation and the Green Revolution

weeks.topic: How energy is produced: renewable and non-renewable sources
objectives: Compare fossil fuels, nuclear and renewable energy
Explain factors affecting energy choice

weeks.topic: Global patterns of energy supply and demand
objectives: Describe global patterns of energy production and consumption
Explain energy security

weeks.topic: Impacts of energy production (detailed specific example)
objectives: Evaluate environmental and social impacts of a specific energy project
Discuss sustainable energy use

weeks.topic: Paper 4 geographical investigations: hypotheses and methodology
objectives: Write testable hypotheses
Select sampling methods and data-collection techniques

weeks.topic: Fieldwork: presenting, analysing and evaluating data
objectives: Choose suitable graphs and maps for fieldwork data
Analyse results and evaluate the reliability of methods

weeks.topic: Extended answers: using detailed specific examples and evaluation
objectives: Structure 7–9 mark answers using place-specific detail
Make supported judgements in evaluation questions

weeks.topic: Exam technique: Section A and Section B in Papers 1 and 2
objectives: Choose questions wisely in Section B
Allocate time by marks and use the resource booklet

weeks.topic: Mock exams: Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 4
objectives: Complete full-length mock papers under exam conditions
Use feedback to update a revision plan

weeks.topic: Review: changing river and coastal environments
objectives: Revise processes, landforms and management examples
Practise annotated diagrams

weeks.topic: Review: changing ecosystems and tectonic hazards
objectives: Revise Antarctica and rainforest threats
Revise earthquake and volcano examples

weeks.topic: Review: climate change
objectives: Revise causes, impacts and responses
Practise evaluation questions

weeks.topic: Review: changing populations and changing towns and cities
objectives: Revise population structures and migration
Revise urban opportunities and management

weeks.topic: Review: development and changing economies
objectives: Revise development indicators and TNCs
Revise tourism impacts

weeks.topic: Review: resource provision and geographical skills
objectives: Revise food and energy topics
Practise map, graph and fieldwork skills

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 1 physical geography
objectives: Answer Section A and two Section B questions
Use detailed specific examples

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 2 human geography
objectives: Answer Section A and two Section B questions
Interpret resources accurately

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 4 geographical investigations
objectives: Apply fieldwork knowledge to two investigation questions
Evaluate methods and conclusions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on the course and next steps in IB or A Level Geography
